- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model overcorrects in next period; apply downward bias of 3–7% to prevent overshoot.
- If forecast mean is significantly above true mean (e.g., >10% over 30d), apply downward adjustment proportional to sentiment volatility (higher sentiment = stronger correction).
- For 30d horizon, model often lags true trend by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment momentum — if sentiment rising, forecast should trend up; if falling, trend down.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to be overly conservative; increase forecast by 3–6% to counteract underreaction.
